title: Forecast Accuracy (Silver Layer)
description: How much can I trust the forecast? NWS forecast accuracy analysis against observed ground truth.

panels.title: Accuracy % (within 2C)
panels.description: Percentage of forecasts where temperature error was within 2 degrees Celsius of actual observation

targets.rawSql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Panel: Overall Accuracy Percentage (within 2C threshold)
-- =============================================================================
-- Purpose: Show what percentage of forecasts were within 2 degrees of actual
-- Logic:
--   1. Join forecasts to observations on valid_time = observation_time (within 30 min)
--   2. Count forecasts where |forecast - observed| <= 2C
--   3. Divide by total to get percentage
-- =============================================================================
WITH forecast_vs_actual AS (
    -- Step 1: Join each forecast to the closest observation
    -- We match forecast valid_time to observation_time within +/- 30 minutes
    -- This accounts for slight timing differences between forecast validity
    -- and when observations are actually recorded
    SELECT
        f.valid_time,
        f.issue_time,
        f.temperature_c AS forecast_temp,
        o.temperature_c AS observed_temp,
        ABS(f.temperature_c - o.temperature_c) AS temp_error
    FROM silver.weather_forecasts f
    INNER JOIN silver.weather_observations o
        ON o.observation_time BETWEEN f.valid_time - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
                                  AND f.valid_time + INTERVAL '30 minutes'

    WHERE f.valid_time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
      -- Exclude rows with DQ flags for clean analysis
      AND (f.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(f.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND (o.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(o.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND f.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
      AND o.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    -- Calculate percentage of forecasts within 2C threshold
    ROUND(
        ((COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE temp_error <= 2.0) * 100.0) /
        NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0))::numeric,
        1
    ) AS "Accuracy %"
FROM forecast_vs_actual;

panels.title: Trustworthy Horizon
panels.description: Maximum lead time bucket where MAE is still under 2C - forecasts beyond this horizon are less reliable

targets.rawSql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Panel: Trustworthy Horizon
-- =============================================================================
-- Purpose: Find the maximum lead time where MAE < 2C (the "reliability cutoff")
-- Logic:
--   1. Calculate MAE for each lead time bucket
--   2. Find the last bucket where MAE is still under 2C threshold
--   3. Return that as "Forecasts reliable up to X hours"
-- =============================================================================
WITH forecast_vs_actual AS (
    SELECT
        f.valid_time,
        f.lead_time_hours,
        f.temperature_c AS forecast_temp,
        o.temperature_c AS observed_temp,
        ABS(f.temperature_c - o.temperature_c) AS temp_error,
        -- Assign to lead time buckets as specified:
        -- 1h: 0-1.5h, 3h: 1.5-4.5h, 6h: 4.5-9h, 12h: 9-18h, 24h: 18-36h, 48h: 36-60h
        CASE
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 1.5 THEN '1'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 4.5 THEN '3'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 9 THEN '6'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 18 THEN '12'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 36 THEN '24'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 60 THEN '48'
            ELSE '48+'
        END AS bucket_hours,
        CASE
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 1.5 THEN 1
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 4.5 THEN 2
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 9 THEN 3
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 18 THEN 4
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 36 THEN 5
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 60 THEN 6
            ELSE 7
        END AS bucket_order
    FROM silver.weather_forecasts f
    INNER JOIN silver.weather_observations o
        ON o.observation_time BETWEEN f.valid_time - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
                                  AND f.valid_time + INTERVAL '30 minutes'

    WHERE f.valid_time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
      AND (f.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(f.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND (o.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(o.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND f.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
      AND o.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
),
mae_by_bucket AS (
    SELECT
        bucket_hours,
        bucket_order,
        AVG(temp_error) AS mae
    FROM forecast_vs_actual
    GROUP BY bucket_hours, bucket_order
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5  -- Need minimum samples for reliability
)
SELECT
    -- Find the last bucket where MAE < 2C
    COALESCE(
        (
            SELECT bucket_hours || ' hours'
            FROM mae_by_bucket
            WHERE mae < 2.0
            ORDER BY bucket_order DESC
            LIMIT 1
        ),
        'N/A'
    ) AS "Reliable Up To";

panels.title: Current Temperature Bias
panels.description: Average signed error over the selected period. Positive = forecast runs warm, Negative = forecast runs cold

targets.rawSql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Panel: Temperature Bias (Mean Error)
-- =============================================================================
-- Purpose: Show systematic bias in forecasts
-- Interpretation:
--   Positive: Forecasts tend to be TOO WARM
--   Negative: Forecasts tend to be TOO COLD
--   Near zero: No systematic bias (ideal)
-- =============================================================================
WITH forecast_vs_actual AS (
    SELECT
        f.temperature_c - o.temperature_c AS temp_bias
    FROM silver.weather_forecasts f
    INNER JOIN silver.weather_observations o
        ON o.observation_time BETWEEN f.valid_time - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
                                  AND f.valid_time + INTERVAL '30 minutes'

    WHERE f.valid_time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
      AND (f.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(f.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND (o.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(o.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND f.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
      AND o.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG(temp_bias)::numeric, 2) AS "Bias"
FROM forecast_vs_actual;

panels.title: Total Comparisons
panels.description: Number of forecast-to-observation comparisons in the selected time range

targets.rawSql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Panel: Total Comparisons Count

-- Purpose: Show sample size for statistical confidence
-- More comparisons = more reliable accuracy metrics

SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS "Comparisons"
FROM silver.weather_forecasts f
INNER JOIN silver.weather_observations o
    ON o.observation_time BETWEEN f.valid_time - INTERVAL '30 minutes'

   AND f.ndp_id = o.ndp_id
WHERE f.valid_time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  AND (f.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(f.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
  AND (o.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(o.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)

  AND o.temperature_c IS NOT NULL;

panels.title: Temperature MAE by Lead Time
panels.description: Mean Absolute Error in temperature forecasts by lead time bucket. Lower is better.

targets.rawSql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Panel: Temperature MAE by Lead Time Bucket
-- =============================================================================
-- Purpose: Show how forecast accuracy degrades with lead time
-- 
-- Lead Time Buckets (as specified):
--   1 hour:  0-1.5h   - Immediate decisions (e.g., "should I bring an umbrella?")
--   3 hours: 1.5-4.5h - Near-term planning (e.g., "outdoor event this afternoon")
--   6 hours: 4.5-9h   - Same-day planning (e.g., "evening activities")
--   12 hours: 9-18h   - Next-day planning (e.g., "tomorrow morning")
--   24 hours: 18-36h  - Tomorrow (e.g., "what to wear tomorrow")
--   48 hours: 36-60h  - Weekend planning (e.g., "outdoor weekend activities")
--
-- MAE (Mean Absolute Error): Average of |forecast - observed|
--   - Ignores direction of error (too warm vs too cold)
--   - Lower values = more accurate forecasts
--   - Typical "good" MAE: < 2C for short-term, < 3C for 24h+
-- =============================================================================
WITH forecast_vs_actual AS (
    SELECT
        f.lead_time_hours,
        ABS(f.temperature_c - o.temperature_c) AS temp_error,
        -- Bucket assignment based on lead time ranges
        CASE
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 1.5 THEN '1 hour'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 4.5 THEN '3 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 9 THEN '6 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 18 THEN '12 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 36 THEN '24 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 60 THEN '48 hours'
            ELSE '48+ hours'
        END AS lead_time_bucket,
        -- For ordering in chart
        CASE
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 1.5 THEN 1
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 4.5 THEN 2
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 9 THEN 3
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 18 THEN 4
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 36 THEN 5
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 60 THEN 6
            ELSE 7
        END AS bucket_order
    FROM silver.weather_forecasts f
    INNER JOIN silver.weather_observations o
        -- Join on time proximity: observation within +/- 30 min of forecast valid_time
        ON o.observation_time BETWEEN f.valid_time - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
                                  AND f.valid_time + INTERVAL '30 minutes'

    WHERE f.valid_time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
      -- Exclude flagged data for clean accuracy analysis
      AND (f.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(f.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND (o.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(o.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND f.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
      AND o.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    lead_time_bucket AS "Lead Time",
    ROUND(AVG(temp_error)::numeric, 2) AS "MAE (C)"
FROM forecast_vs_actual
GROUP BY lead_time_bucket, bucket_order
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3  -- Minimum samples for meaningful average
ORDER BY bucket_order;

panels.title: Temperature Bias by Lead Time
panels.description: Mean signed error (forecast - observed). Positive = forecast too warm, Negative = forecast too cold

targets.rawSql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Panel: Temperature Bias by Lead Time Bucket
-- =============================================================================
-- Purpose: Reveal systematic forecast biases that vary with lead time
-- 
-- Bias = Mean(forecast - observed)
--   Positive bias: Forecasts tend to be TOO WARM
--   Negative bias: Forecasts tend to be TOO COLD
--   Near zero: No systematic bias (ideal)
--
-- Use Cases:
--   - Identify if NWS consistently over/under predicts temperature
--   - See if bias changes with forecast horizon
--   - Calibration: Could adjust forecasts by subtracting bias
-- =============================================================================
WITH forecast_vs_actual AS (
    SELECT
        f.lead_time_hours,
        f.temperature_c - o.temperature_c AS temp_bias,  -- Signed error
        CASE
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 1.5 THEN '1 hour'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 4.5 THEN '3 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 9 THEN '6 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 18 THEN '12 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 36 THEN '24 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 60 THEN '48 hours'
            ELSE '48+ hours'
        END AS lead_time_bucket,
        CASE
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 1.5 THEN 1
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 4.5 THEN 2
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 9 THEN 3
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 18 THEN 4
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 36 THEN 5
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 60 THEN 6
            ELSE 7
        END AS bucket_order
    FROM silver.weather_forecasts f
    INNER JOIN silver.weather_observations o
        ON o.observation_time BETWEEN f.valid_time - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
                                  AND f.valid_time + INTERVAL '30 minutes'

    WHERE f.valid_time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
      AND (f.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(f.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND (o.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(o.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND f.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
      AND o.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    lead_time_bucket AS "Lead Time",
    ROUND(AVG(temp_bias)::numeric, 2) AS "Bias (C)"
FROM forecast_vs_actual
GROUP BY lead_time_bucket, bucket_order
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY bucket_order;

panels.title: Forecast vs Actual Temperature
panels.description: Overlay of forecast temperature and observed temperature over time

targets.rawSql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Panel: Forecast vs Actual Temperature Time Series
-- =============================================================================
-- Purpose: Visual comparison of forecast and observed temperatures
-- 
-- Logic:
--   1. Get hourly forecast values (using latest issue for each valid_time)
--   2. Get hourly observed values (averaged per hour)
--   3. Return both series for overlay comparison
--
-- Temperature Unit Conversion:
--   Uses dashboard variable ${temp_unit} to toggle Celsius/Fahrenheit
--   Formula: F = (C * 9/5) + 32
-- =============================================================================
WITH hourly_forecasts AS (
    -- Get the latest forecast issued for each valid hour
    -- Using DISTINCT ON to get one forecast per valid_time
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (date_trunc('hour', valid_time))
        date_trunc('hour', valid_time) AS time,
        CASE
            WHEN '${temp_unit}' = 'Fahrenheit'
            THEN (temperature_c * 9.0/5.0) + 32
            ELSE temperature_c
        END AS temperature
    FROM silver.weather_forecasts
    WHERE valid_time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
      AND (dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND temperature_c IS NOT NULL
    ORDER BY date_trunc('hour', valid_time), issue_time DESC
),
hourly_observations AS (
    -- Average observed temperature per hour
    SELECT
        date_trunc('hour', observation_time) AS time,
        CASE
            WHEN '${temp_unit}' = 'Fahrenheit'
            THEN (AVG(temperature_c) * 9.0/5.0) + 32
            ELSE AVG(temperature_c)
        END AS temperature
    FROM silver.weather_observations
    WHERE observation_time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
      AND (dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND temperature_c IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY date_trunc('hour', observation_time)
)
SELECT
    COALESCE(f.time, o.time) AS time,
    f.temperature AS "Forecast",
    o.temperature AS "Actual"
FROM hourly_forecasts f
FULL OUTER JOIN hourly_observations o ON f.time = o.time
WHERE COALESCE(f.time, o.time) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY time;

panels.title: Wind Speed MAE by Lead Time

targets.rawSql:
-- =============================================================================

--

--   - Local terrain effects

    SELECT
        f.lead_time_hours,

        CASE
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 1.5 THEN '1 hour'

            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 18 THEN '12 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 36 THEN '24 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 60 THEN '48 hours'
            ELSE '48+ hours'
        END AS lead_time_bucket,
        CASE
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 1.5 THEN 1
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 4.5 THEN 2
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 9 THEN 3
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 18 THEN 4
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 36 THEN 5
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 60 THEN 6
            ELSE 7
        END AS bucket_order
    FROM silver.weather_forecasts f
    INNER JOIN silver.weather_observations o
        ON o.observation_time BETWEEN f.valid_time - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
                                  AND f.valid_time + INTERVAL '30 minutes'

    WHERE f.valid_time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
      AND (f.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(f.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND (o.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(o.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)

FROM forecast_vs_actual
GROUP BY lead_time_bucket, bucket_order
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY bucket_order;

panels.title: Temperature Error Over Time
panels.description: Signed temperature error (forecast - actual) over time. Shows systematic biases and patterns.

targets.rawSql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Panel: Temperature Error Over Time
-- =============================================================================
-- Purpose: Show how forecast error varies over time
-- 
-- Signed error helps identify:
--   - Diurnal patterns (worse at night? worse during day?)
--   - Weather-dependent accuracy (worse during frontal passages?)
--   - Seasonal variations
--
-- Color coding: Bars colored by error magnitude/direction
--   Green zone: -1C to +1C (excellent)
--   Yellow: +/- 2C (acceptable)
--   Red: beyond +/- 3C (needs attention)
-- =============================================================================
WITH hourly_errors AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('hour', f.valid_time) AS time,
        AVG(f.temperature_c - o.temperature_c) AS error
    FROM silver.weather_forecasts f
    INNER JOIN silver.weather_observations o
        ON o.observation_time BETWEEN f.valid_time - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
                                  AND f.valid_time + INTERVAL '30 minutes'

    WHERE f.valid_time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
      AND (f.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(f.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND (o.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(o.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND f.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
      AND o.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY date_trunc('hour', f.valid_time)
)
SELECT
    time,
    ROUND(error::numeric, 2) AS "Error (C)"
FROM hourly_errors
ORDER BY time;

panels.title: Accuracy Summary by Lead Time
panels.description: Comprehensive accuracy metrics for each lead time bucket

targets.rawSql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Panel: Comprehensive Accuracy Summary Table
-- =============================================================================
-- Purpose: Detailed statistics for each lead time bucket
-- 
-- Metrics shown:
--   - MAE: Mean Absolute Error (how far off on average)
--   - Bias: Mean signed error (systematic over/under prediction)
--   - RMSE: Root Mean Square Error (penalizes large errors more)
--   - Accuracy %: Percentage within 2C threshold
--   - Sample N: Number of comparisons (statistical reliability)
-- =============================================================================
WITH forecast_vs_actual AS (
    SELECT
        f.lead_time_hours,
        f.temperature_c AS forecast_temp,
        o.temperature_c AS observed_temp,
        f.temperature_c - o.temperature_c AS temp_bias,
        ABS(f.temperature_c - o.temperature_c) AS temp_error,
        POWER(f.temperature_c - o.temperature_c, 2) AS temp_error_sq,
        CASE
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 1.5 THEN '1 hour'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 4.5 THEN '3 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 9 THEN '6 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 18 THEN '12 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 36 THEN '24 hours'
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 60 THEN '48 hours'
            ELSE '48+ hours'
        END AS lead_time_bucket,
        CASE
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 1.5 THEN 1
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 4.5 THEN 2
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 9 THEN 3
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 18 THEN 4
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 36 THEN 5
            WHEN f.lead_time_hours <= 60 THEN 6
            ELSE 7
        END AS bucket_order
    FROM silver.weather_forecasts f
    INNER JOIN silver.weather_observations o
        ON o.observation_time BETWEEN f.valid_time - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
                                  AND f.valid_time + INTERVAL '30 minutes'

    WHERE f.valid_time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
      AND (f.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(f.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND (o.dq_flags IS NULL OR array_length(o.dq_flags, 1) IS NULL)
      AND f.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
      AND o.temperature_c IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    lead_time_bucket AS "Lead Time",
    ROUND(AVG(temp_error)::numeric, 2) AS "MAE (C)",
    ROUND(AVG(temp_bias)::numeric, 2) AS "Bias (C)",
    ROUND(SQRT(AVG(temp_error_sq))::numeric, 2) AS "RMSE (C)",
    ROUND(
        ((COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE temp_error <= 2.0) * 100.0) /
        NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0))::numeric,
        1
    ) AS "Within 2C %",
    COUNT(*) AS "Samples"
FROM forecast_vs_actual
GROUP BY lead_time_bucket, bucket_order
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY bucket_order;
